extracted.intended_audience: readers tracking corporate responses to LGBTQ+ issues (LGBTQ+ community, allies, and general public interested in corporate accountability)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examples about how a corporation crafts and issues a public statement in response to controversy/backlash (here focused on LGBTQ+ inclusion). Includes what to say, what to emphasise, and examples of evasive vs. specific language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit inclusive language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear, explicit inclusive phrasing such as “Chick-fil-A embraces all people, regardless of race, gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or gender identity.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out the protected categories you mean to include rather than using vague phrasing. The article quotes the exact language used by Chick‑fil‑A as an example of an inclusive automated response; such explicit listing signals inclusion to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: State commitment to DEI
rubrics_metrics.description: Assert an organisational commitment to Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI) as part of the response (e.g., “Chick-fil-A, Inc. is committed to being Better at Together by embedding Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI) in everything we do”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming DEI and signalling it is embedded in operations frames the statement as proactive rather than merely reactive. Provide concrete DEI framing rather than a single-sentence platitude when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference corporate social responsibility (CSR) pillars
rubrics_metrics.description: Tie the response to established CSR pillars or programmes (example: ‘Caring for People, Caring for our Communities, Caring for Others through our Food, and Caring for our Planet’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking inclusive language to existing CSR pillars shows the statement aligns with broader company priorities; list the pillars and, if relevant, how they inform action or decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pledge of respectful treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Affirm the company’s service tradition and promise to treat every person with ‘honour, dignity and respect’ regardless of belief, race, creed, sexual orientation or gender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterate customer‑facing behavioural norms (how staff and stores should treat people) to reassure stakeholders about day‑to‑day conduct and culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid taking a political policy position
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly avoid engaging in public policy debates about contested issues (example from 2012: ‘our intent is to leave the policy debate over same-sex marriage to the government and political arena’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies may choose to deflect policy debates to government to appear neutral; state this stance clearly if that is the intent. Note this can be perceived as noncommittal by some audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge past controversies and outline changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise historical criticisms (donations, past statements) and, where applicable, announce concrete policy or strategy changes (example: announcing a new charitable-donations strategy that cuts funding to certain groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admitting past actions and describing specific changes (dates, amounts, new criteria) helps rebuild credibility. Vague or absent acknowledgement leaves space for continued criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address misinformation and encourage fact-seeking
rubrics_metrics.description: Push back against misinformation by urging the public to ‘seek the truth before rushing to ill-informed judgment’ and provide factual context about who the company serves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the statement to correct false narratives and supply verifiable facts (e.g., beneficiary counts, program descriptions). Avoid accusatory tone; focus on evidence and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent about charitable-donation strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the company’s charitable-donation strategy and its goals (example quote: ‘provide maximum impact and maximum clarity with our charitable dollars’), especially if donations have been the source of controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than evasive phrasing, offer specifics: criteria for grants, recipient vetting, and changes in giving priorities. The article shows spokespeople sometimes respond evasively; transparency reduces scepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use consistent, documented messaging (including automated replies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deploy standardized, documented statements for consistency (the corporate office ‘issued an automated statement that appears when complaints are submitted through its website’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated or templated responses ensure uniformity across channels, but should be reviewed for tone and specificity so they don't appear formulaic or dismissive in sensitive contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid evasive or non-answer responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not evade direct questions about past actions; the article notes a spokesperson ‘seemingly evaded the question’ when asked whether donations were cut because of anti‑LGBTQ stances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evasive language undermines trust. If full disclosure is not possible, explain why and provide as much verifiable information as permitted. Offer timelines for follow-up when necessary.
